topIssues.title: op-supervisor: consider `panic` if rewind would affect `finalized`
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18801/changes#diff-bef9998039325b0040ecbc60a17787c433af2bf87a6cec2d7263ac9089d1e150R198-R199

current implementation of chain rewind allows for finalized heads to revert. This technical ability is reasonable, but in a product sense, it would be unacceptable to ever revert the finalized head.

Consider crashing the application via `panic` if it should ever determine that a revert of finalized is called for.

topIssues.title: contracts: Enable CANNON_KONA as respected game type after Kona audit
topIssues.author: stevennevins
topIssues.body:
After the Kona audit completes, update the `RESPECTED_GAME_TYPE_CANNON_KONA` dev feature flag to switch the respected game type from CANNON to CANNON_KONA.

  The flag infrastructure was added in TODO(PR#) and currently validates that the respected game type is CANNON or PERMISSIONED_CANNON. This issue tracks the one-line follow-up to activate it.

  ## Changes needed

  In `OPContractsManagerV2._apply()`, replace the current validation with:
  1. Set `_cfg.startingRespectedGameType = GameTypes.CANNON_KONA`
  2. Validate that CANNON_KONA is enabled in `disputeGameConfigs`

  Update tests in `OPContractsManagerV2_RespectedGameTypeCannonKona_Test`:
  - Allowed: CANNON_KONA (flag overrides input)
  - Rejected: CANNON, PERMISSIONED_CANNON (no longer valid when flag is on)
  - Add upgrade path test

  ## Blocked by

  - Kona audit completion

topIssues.title: proofs: Ensure DG created before rollup L1 genesis is supported
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
As a follow-up to https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19114, introduce an acceptance-test that covers the case where a dispute game was created before the L2 genesis (and its L1 origin).

The test should target a devstack environment running supernode and supernode+2chain-interop. However, none of the existing devstack presets currently support the ability to create dispute games before L2 genesis, so this functionality will need to be implemented first.

topPRs.title: feat(kona): preconfirmation tracking for sequencer leadership transfer
topPRs.author: niran
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds a preconfirmation tracking subsystem to the kona sequencer that subscribes to upstream flashblocks via WebSocket and tracks ordered transaction sequences per parent hash
- On conductor-based leadership transfer, the new leader injects previously preconfirmed transactions into its first block's payload attributes, preserving user-visible transaction ordering
- Gated behind a `preconfirmations` feature flag with CLI args (`--sequencer.preconfirmations`, `--sequencer.preconfirmation-flashblocks-url`, `--sequencer.preconfirmation-ttl`)

### Key design decisions

- **Tracks ordering, not individual txs**: Flashblocks are differential — each carries only new transactions. The subscriber appends each flashblock's transactions to a flattened `Vec<Bytes>` per parent hash, preserving the committed ordering.
- **Consume-once semantics**: `take_transactions()` drains the entry on read, preventing re-injection of the node's own flashblocks if it stays subscribed after becoming leader.
- **Conductor-gated**: The tracker is only created when both preconfirmations and conductor are enabled, since leadership transfer requires conductor.
- **Parent hash matching**: Preconfirmed transactions are injected only into the block with the matching parent hash. During clock catch-up, subsequent blocks have different parent hashes and receive no injection.
- **Graceful degradation**: If the flashblocks WS disconnects, the sequencer keeps producing blocks normally. Reconnection is automatic.

### New files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `preconfirmation/mod.rs` | Module re-exports |
| `preconfirmation/config.rs` | `PreconfirmationConfig` struct |
| `preconfirmation/tracker.rs` | `PreconfirmationTracker` with 8 unit tests |
| `preconfirmation/subscriber.rs` | `FlashblocksSubscriber` WebSocket consumer |

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p kona-node-service --features preconfirmations` compiles
- [x] `cargo check -p kona-node-service` (without feature) compiles
- [x] `cargo check -p kona-node` compiles
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-node-service --features preconfirmations` — no warnings from new code
- [x] `cargo nextest run --package kona-node-service --features preconfirmations` — 121/121 tests pass
- [x] Unit tests for `PreconfirmationTracker`: start_sequence, append, take (consume-once), TTL expiry, payload_id mismatch rejection, start replaces existing, nonexistent parent
- [x] Integration test: preconfirmations injected only into correct block during catch-up (not into subsequent blocks)
- [x] Integration test: preconfirmations injected even when `no_tx_pool` is true (sequencer drift exceeded)

topPRs.title: feat: add scaffolding for making kona the default respected game type
topPRs.author: stevennevins
topPRs.body:
**Description**                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   
  Adds the `RESPECTED_GAME_TYPE_CANNON_KONA` dev feature flag to OPCM. When enabled, the flag validates that `startingRespectedGameType` is `CANNON` or `PERMISSIONED_CANNON` during `deploy()` and `upgrade()` (via            
  `_apply()`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                        
  This is preparatory infrastructure — after the Kona audit, the check will be updated to set `CANNON_KONA` as the respected game type instead. DevFeatures are blocked on mainnet by `OPContractsManagerContainer`, so this has
   no production impact.

  Changes:
  - New `DevFeatures.RESPECTED_GAME_TYPE_CANNON_KONA` constant (nibble 5)
  - Validation check in `OPContractsManagerV2._apply()` between DelayedWETH and AnchorStateRegistry upgrades
  - New `OPContractsManagerV2_InvalidRespectedGameType` error
  - Env var reader, test infra wiring, semver bump

  **Tests**

  Three new tests in `OPContractsManagerV2_RespectedGameTypeCannonKona_Test`:
  - `test_deploy_flagOn_allowsCannon_succeeds` — CANNON input passes validation
  - `test_deploy_flagOn_allowsPermissionedCannon_succeeds` — PERMISSIONED_CANNON input passes validation
  - `test_deploy_flagOn_rejectsCannonKona_reverts` — CANNON_KONA input reverts (not yet allowed)

  Flag-off regression covered by existing `OPContractsManagerV2_Deploy_Test`.

  **Additional context**

  Follow-up after Kona audit tracked in #19116. TODOs in the contract and test file are tagged with the issue number.

  **Metadata**
  - Fixes #18640
  - Contributes to #19116

topPRs.title: op-acceptance: Add test for next super root not being available.
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Add a test to ensure that the challenger calculates the correct transition when the next superroot is unknown but the first chain does have the next block available on L1.  It should only transition to the invalid hash on the second chain block.

The FPP tests were moved to their own package so they can run in parallel with the other proofs tests since they're pretty long running but can't run in parallel on the same devnet.


**Tests**

Confirmed the test reproduces the original bug by re-introducing the issue into the challenger provider and confirming the FPP run detects the difference.

**Metadata**

fixes #18643

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): pull latest superchain config on startup
topPRs.author: 0xPenryn
topPRs.body:
<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

Updates the `reth-optimism-chainspec` crate, adding functionality to pull the latest chain configuration directly from the Superchain Registry. If the Superchain Registry is unreachable, it will fall back to the local chain configurations and follow the existing behavior.

This functionality is enabled by the `pull-superchain-configs` feature in the `reth-optimism-chainspec` crate, and does not modify the current functionality when the `superchain-configs` feature is used instead.

**Tests**

No tests added, but happy-path is confirmed to work by actually running it. I'm not familiar with writing tests that mock HTTP requests -- would be happy to see them added!

**Additional context**

With this PR, `op-reth` doesn't need to cut a new release to reflect updates to the Superchain Registry; rather, the node operator simply needs to restart `op-reth` and it will pull the latest config. For chains that do not follow the Superchain upgrade timestamps, this significantly streamlines the process for hardfork enablements (or other configuration changes) to be reflected by node operators.

Before this PR:

- Submit + merge PR to Superchain Registry
- Submit + merge PR to `op-reth` pulling latest Superchain Registry
- Wait for `op-reth` release
- Tell node operators to update to new version of `op-reth`

After this PR:

- Submit + merge PR to Superchain Registry
- Tell node operators to restart `op-reth`

topPRs.title: Supernode: Faster Processing with Backoff
topPRs.author: axelKingsley
topPRs.body:
# What
Adaptive tick rate for interop activity

- Lowered tickerPeriod from 500ms → 50ms for fast progress when data is available
- Added backoffPeriod (1s) when chains aren't ready, preventing busy-waiting
- Extracted the error sleep into errorBackoffPeriod (2s) for clarity
- progressAndRecord(): Now returns (verifiedAdvanced bool, err error) to signal whether the verified timestamp was advanced, driving the backoff decision
- Unit tests now assert advancement
